articles.title: Jaylen Brown injury update: A crucial Sixers concern emerges after his scary moment against Miami Heat
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown left the Philadelphia 76ers' 111-104 win over the Miami Heat on Wednesday night with left hamstring tightness and did not return for the
articles.body: Jaylen Brown left the Philadelphia 76ers' 111-104 win over the Miami Heat on Wednesday night with left hamstring tightness and did not return for the second half. Brown grabbed at his leg in the final seconds of the second quarter and went straight to the locker room. Brown strained the same hamstring last week. Head coach Nick Nurse said Brown will undergo imaging, with an update expected Thursday. Philadelphia still won the NBA Cup game, and it did so without Joel Embiid.What is Jaylen Brown's injury status after leaving the Heat game?The trouble started right after a step-back jumper. Brown pulled up short, waved toward the bench, and left with 1.2 seconds on the clock, ahead of the rest of the team and frustrated. The 76ers soon confirmed the left hamstring was re-aggravated and Brown was done for the night.The 76ers guard was having a quiet night anyway. Over 17 minutes of work, Brown finished with six points, one rebound and one assist on 2-of-8 shooting, far below the season marks of 21.4 points per game and 54.5 percent from the field.Nurse offered little detail afterward. "He'll get some imaging," the coach said, "and we'll get the update tomorrow."Brown went down in just the second game back from a two-game absence with a left hamstring strain. The return came in a 128-111 loss to Portland, and the Heat game was the very next one.Soft-tissue injuries are piling up around the league, and the 76ers may treat this one as a precaution. Hamstrings are tricky, though, and a second flare-up inside a week gives Philadelphia reason to move slowly. Brown matters well beyond November, since the playoffs are where a two-way wing like Brown is hardest to replace, and the team has little to gain from rushing a return.How the 76ers held off Miami without BrownMiami arrived at full strength on a seven-game winning streak, and Philadelphia was already short-handed with Embiid out. The margin for error was thin, and it got thinner the moment Brown headed down the tunnel.The 76ers carried a solid lead into halftime, and the third quarter finished even at 28-28 with Brown in the locker room. Early in the fourth, they took control.Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points. LeBron James posted a triple-double of 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds, running much of the offense once Brown left. V.J. Edgecombe added 18 points, six rebounds and five assists.Edgecombe's work at both ends was a big part of the fourth-quarter push. Maxey, James and Edgecombe combined for 73 of the team's 111 points, a heavy load for three players on a night when two others were sidelined.Indiana is next on the schedule, followed by Houston, so the scan results will shape the rotation almost immediately.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: John Blackwell ends his cold streak, leads No. 16 Duke to statement win over Silas Demary Jr. and No. 10 UConn
articles.summary: The Blue Devils had been 0-2 against ranked opponents this season before Wednesday's win.
articles.body:
The No. 16 Duke Blue Devils bested the No. 10 UConn Huskies 77-63 on Wednesday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

Duke entered the game 4-2, with both losses coming against ranked opponents. UConn was 4-1, but coming off a loss against No. 12 Arizona.

Duke senior guard John Blackwell had registered 11 points or fewer in three straight games. Against SIU Edwardsville, Blackwell went 1-for-7 from the field and finished with just three points.

The guard finally looked like the player Duke has needed him to be on Wednesday night. Blackwell led the team with 25 points on 7-of-11 shooting, including five of his six 3-point attempts. He scored 20 in the second half as the Blue Devils held on to their lead throughout.

Patrick Ngongba II finished with 17 points and 11 rebounds.

One major storyline for Duke is Dame Sarr's health. He landed awkwardly after going up for a block with 5:12 left in the game. Sarr limped off the court and did not return. He celebrated the win with teammates after the game.

While UConn lost, guard Silas Demary Jr. finished with 25 points. He dominated the first half but went ice cold in the second, like many of his teammates. The Huskies shot just 31% from the field, including a 30% clip from beyond the arc.

Na'jai Hines and Braylon Mullins both got into foul trouble and fouled out before the end of the game. Colben Landrew struggled from the field, finishing 2-for-13.

Duke is now 5-2 and will be off until next Tuesday as the Blue Devils go on the road for a huge matchup against No. 3 Florida. UConn drops to 4-2 and will return home Monday to host Rider.

At one point, there was concern that Solo Ball would miss the entire season because of offseason surgery to repair multiple torn ligaments in his left wrist.

The guard suffered the injury in December 2025, but at the time it was thought to be just a sprain, and he played through it. After the season, an MRI showed multiple torn ligaments, and he was given a nine-month recovery timeline in May.

Ball recovered faster than expected and opted not to take a medical redshirt for the 2026-2027 season, especially with the new 5-for-5 eligibility policy.

The Huskies guard was made available for Wednesday night's game. He checked in with 12:52 left in the first half.

In his debut, Ball finished with seven points off the bench. He was 2-of-9 from the field, including 1-of-6 from deep. Ball added 2 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 steal.

articles.title: LeBron James gets real about his role on the 76ers and knowing when to step up
articles.summary: LeBron James knows he can still carry the 76ers whenever he's needed.
articles.body:
LeBron James just had his arguably best performance of the 2026-27 NBA season so far against the Miami Heat on Wednesday. It was his first triple-double in a Philadelphia 76ers uniform, getting 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists. This was a big shift for the 76ers because they needed another go-to guy without Joel Embiid.

Of course, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown still played well, but a tough game against the Miami Heat required him to dust off the superhero cape. It was a much-needed performance to bounce back from the loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , and it was a result that snapped the Heat's seven-game winning streak.

LeBron James admits he can still be the hero for the 76ers when needed

For the past 24 seasons, people have become familiar with James and how he carries his teams. Now that he is 41, it is fair not to expect that to happen all the time. However, there are times when James can still pull off a big performance just like what he did on Wednesday against Miami.

Philadelphia has been hyped up as one of the best teams in the league this season, and for good reason. The likes of Maxey and Brown have truly led the team in production, but at the same time, James has been mostly in the background as a playmaker and tertiary scorer.

At times, James would even be behind V.J. Edgecombe in the pecking order of scorers. However, that was not the case against Miami because he stepped up across the board as a scorer, defender, and playmaker. He admits that this won't happen all the time, but he is willing to step up when he is needed.

"I don't think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club... If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that," James said in his post-game interview after leading the 76ers past the Heat .

This also prompted Maxey to react to what just happened with James leading the charge. As the younger star player for the 76ers, he would appreciate it if James did this all the time because his job would be easier as a result.

"Dust it off then! Earlier in the game, he was telling me he was tired; I said, 'Well, you don't have time to be tired'. He does a good job of just managing the game. Like, he knows when he needs to score, he knows when he needs to pass, you know we're gonna need a lot from him. I know he's seasoned, but we expect a lot of him," Maxey said in his own post-game interview .

articles.title: Dame Sarr to get MRI following Duke basketball's win over UConn
articles.summary: Dame Sarr will be getting an MRI after appearing to land awkwardly on his left leg in the second half of the UConn game. Here's what we know.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — Dame Sarr will be getting an MRI following Duke basketball 's 77-63 win over UConn on Wednesday, Nov. 25, coach Jon Scheyer said after the game.

Sarr limped off to the bench with 5:30 left in the game after attempting to block a Solo Ball shot and appearing to land awkwardly on his left leg. The sophomore was looked at by trainers on the bench and was seen standing in the bench area but did not return to the court

"We're going to get an MRI, check on him, and go from there," Scheyer said.

Sarr finished the night with six points while going 1 for 5 from the field and a perfect 4 for 4 from the charity stripe. He added eight rebounds and a block. He was the primary defender on Braylon Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. for much of the night.

Check out our Duke basketball vs UConn photo gallery, best images

"(He) had an incredible game," Scheyer said. "Chasing (Braylon) Mullins all over the place."

Sarr has started in six of Duke 's games this season and is averaging 10 points per game.

Duke is back in action against Florida in the ACC/SEC Challenge in Gainesville on Tuesday, Dec. 1.

Anna Snyder covers Duke for The Fayetteville Observer as part of the USA TODAY Network. Reach her at asnyder@gannett.com or follow her @annaesnydr on X.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo’s Warning to LeBron James Comes Back to Bite Him as 76ers Snap Heat’s 7-Game Win Streak
articles.summary: Don’t poke the bear, especially when the bear is LeBron James. Bam Adebayo had a playful warning for his good friend after LeBron chose the Philadelphia 76er...
articles.body:
Don't poke the bear, especially when the bear is LeBron James.

Bam Adebayo had a playful warning for his good friend after LeBron chose the Philadelphia 76ers over the Miami Heat in free agency, but James had the last laugh in their first matchup of the 2026-27 season.

James delivered a triple-double with 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists as the 76ers defeated Miami 111-104 on Wednesday night. The victory also ended the Heat's seven-game winning streak, giving Philadelphia a memorable result in the first meeting between the former Olympic teammates since James chose to take his talents to Philadelphia.

Adebayo still had a productive night, finishing with 17 points and 11 rebounds. But his team could not stop James and the 76ers from securing the win.

When James chose Philadelphia over Miami during the offseason, Adebayo made it clear that their friendship would not stop him from competing against the four-time NBA champion.

Speaking to reporters during a community back-to-school event in Miami on July 28, Adebayo revealed the message he sent James after learning of his decision. However, he first made sure to clarify that there were no hard feelings.

"There ain't no disappointment," Adebayo said, per the Miami Herald. "To me, you should always be happy for a person and their decision. He made a decision where he feels like it's his best situation to win. And I feel like I'm a good friend of LeBron's."

The Heat star then revealed the playful warning he had delivered privately. "Like I told him in the message, I'm going to bust his a**," Adebayo added. "So, it's going to be an exciting season. I'm excited for the East. We got a whole new turnaround in the East. So, it's going to be exciting this year."

The two developed a friendship through their time with Team USA, sharing the court during the 2024 Paris Olympics. Both played important roles in the Americans' gold-medal run, fostering a relationship that extends beyond their NBA careers.

That made Adebayo's message less about resentment over James choosing another team and more about the competitive banter between friends. Still, the first opportunity to back up those words arrived Wednesday, and James made sure Philadelphia came away with the victory.

LeBron James answers with Triple-Double as 76ers end Miami's win streak

James delivered his best performance of the season yet, recording 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in Philadelphia's 111-104 win. It was his first triple-double as a member of the 76ers and the 126th of his regular-season career.

At 41 years and 330 days old, James also became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double.

The veteran forward took over during the second quarter, scoring 14 consecutive points to help Philadelphia turn a three-point deficit into a halftime lead. He finished the night shooting 9-of-15 from the field and 4-of-6 from beyond the arc.

Tyrese Maxey provided another major contribution with 30 points and six assists, helping the 76ers withstand Miami's attempts to get back into the game. Philadelphia was also without Joel Embiid, who missed his second consecutive game because of illness, while Jaylen Brown exited after the first half with left hamstring tightness.

Miami had its own standout performer in Giannis Antetokounmpo , who recorded 32 points and 14 rebounds. Adebayo added his double-double, while Davion Mitchell contributed 20 points and 10 assists.

However, the Heat could not overcome Philadelphia's offense and could not extend their winning streak to eight games.

The result improved the 76ers to 15-4 and 2-1 in NBA Cup group play, while Miami also fell to 2-1 in East Group B. Both teams remain in contention for a place in the knockout rounds.

Adebayo may have to wait for another opportunity to make good on his warning, but James has already delivered the first response. The two friends will meet again during the regular season, giving the Heat center another chance to challenge the newest Sixers star.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa Makes 4-Word Statement as Wizards Rookie Gains Momentum
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards are getting a glimpse of what AJ Dybantsa can become.The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is finding his footing after an inju...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards are getting a glimpse of what AJ Dybantsa can become.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is finding his footing after an injury-delayed start to his rookie season. And the 19-year-old appears to have a particular mentality about his development.

Dybantsa took to Instagram on Wednesday, November 25, to share an extensive photo carousel documenting his recent weeks with the Wizards.

The collection of photographs featured everything from game action to pregame and postgame moments, opening with a photograph from a press conference.

"In competition wit myself," Dybantsa wrote in the caption.

The post quickly generated more than 21,000 likes within approximately an hour of being published, with several fans campaigning for Dybantsa to win NBA Rookie of the Year in the comments section.

"DC legend in the making," one Instagram user wrote.

The post came less than 24 hours after Dybantsa delivered one of the most complete performances of his young NBA career.

Wizards' AJ Dybantsa Gaining Momentum in Rookie Season

Dybantsa finished with 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists in Washington's 131-116 loss to the Boston Celtics on Tuesday, November 24.

The performance came against the franchise Dybantsa grew up rooting for. The Brockton, Massachusetts, native had 10 points in the first half before helping Washington make things interesting in the fourth quarter.

The Wizards trimmed a 31-point halftime deficit to five points late in the game before Boston pulled away.

Washington had won three consecutive games entering the matchup.

More encouraging for the Wizards is the variety of ways Dybantsa has been contributing lately.

The rookie registered 20 points, 10 rebounds and six assists against the Chicago Bulls on Friday before contributing 16 points, eight rebounds and six assists in Sunday's 116-96 win over the Orlando Magic.

It's a significant progression from the opening weeks of the season.

As Heavy previously reported , Washington gradually increased Dybantsa's workload after he missed the opening four games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

AJ Dybantsa Climbs in NBA Rookie of the Year Conversation

Dybantsa's recent performances haven't gone unnoticed nationally, either.

The Wizards rookie moved up to No. 4 in the NBA's latest Kia Rookie Ladder , published Wednesday.

Through his first 15 career games, Dybantsa is averaging 16.7 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.1 assists while shooting 42% from the field, according to Basketball Reference .

The former BYU standout also reached an interesting franchise milestone against Boston.

Dybantsa's 251 points through his first 15 games tied former Wizards star John Wall for the fourth-most in franchise history over that span, according to Sports Illustrated .

There is plenty of competition for Rookie of the Year, with Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. moving into the top spot in the latest NBA rankings.

Dybantsa, meanwhile, has recorded at least six assists in each of his last three games.

The scoring was expected. His emergence as a playmaker adds another dimension to what the Wizards can build around their No. 1 pick.

articles.title: Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo can’t lie about LeBron James’ vibrant play with 76ers
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat saw their seven-game winning streak get snapped by the Philadelphia 76ers, 111-104, in the NBA Cup at Xfinity Mobil...
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat saw their seven-game winning streak get snapped by the Philadelphia 76ers , 111-104, in the NBA Cup at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Wednesday.

The Heat could not capitalize despite the 76ers playing without Joel Embiid, who was nursing an illness, and Jaylen Brown exiting in the first half due to a hamstring injury.

LeBron James dismantled the Heat with his first triple-double with the 76ers. James tallied 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists. He shot 9-of-15 from the field, including 4-of-6 from three-point range.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

After the game, Antetokounmpo acknowledged James' impressive stint with the 76ers, as reported by the Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

"I'm not gonna lie. It looks like he's having fun. It doesn't feel like he's 41 years old. He gets to his spot. He's able to play the game that he wants to play. Dictate the game for himself and for his teammates," said Antetokounmpo.

"He's still being himself. But as I said, the most important thing is he looks like he's having fun. When he's knocking down deep threes like that, he's kind of hard to guard."

The four-time MVP is averaging 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists, and 1.1 steals in 32.7 minutes. He recently stated that the 76ers are a "fun group."

Antetokounmpo had 32 points, 14 rebounds, four assists, and two steals. He shot 11-of-18 from the field and 10-of-13 from the free-throw line.

Davion Mitchell added 20 points, four rebounds, and 10 assists, while Bam Adebayo tallied 17 points, 11 rebounds, and three assists.

The Heat fell to 10-7, while the 76ers improved to 15-4.

Miami will try to bounce back against the New York Knicks on Friday.

articles.title: Analysis: No. 19 BYU rides historic 3-point performance to outlast Providence in Maui finale
articles.summary: The Cougars’ 38 attempted triples were the most in Maui Invitational history.
articles.body:
LAHAINA, Hawaii — For the first two days of BYU's stay at the Maui Invitational, it appeared as if the Cougars had left all of their shooting back on the mainland.

Against Washington and Ole Miss, BYU shot just 11 of 51 (22%) from 3-point range, with Cougar players not named Collin Chandler providing just five of those makes.

For a tournament famous for being very shooter-friendly, Kevin Young's crew certainly wasn't seeing any sunny results.

But the soft rims of the Lahaina Civic Center finally came to BYU's aid on Wednesday, as the Cougars defeated the Providence Friars thanks to 17 made 3-pointers.

Considering the 85-82 final score, BYU needed every last one of those triples.

The Cougars' 38 attempts from beyond the arc set a new single-game Maui Invitational record, and the 17 makes tied the 2014 Cougars for the event's second-highest mark.

Somewhere out there, Chase Fischer is smiling.

"It was more of a BYU-style win, I would say," Young told reporters postgame. "That was a big message coming in. We wanted to try to impose our will in terms of how we want to play and not be so reactive, which I thought we did a good job of that."

After going silent offensively in the second half of Tuesday's loss to Ole Miss, the Cougars bounced back in a major way against Providence and its top-15 rated defense, as they torched the Friars for 1.32 points per possession and 19 assists on 28 made field goals.

Providence was surrendering just 64 points per game before Wednesday. BYU bested that number by 21, largely thanks to its persistent perimeter attack, and doing so after having struggled mightily against a stylistically-similar Ole Miss defense.

Just 24 hours after coughing up 23 turnovers to the Rebels, the Rob Wright III-less Cougars cut their giveaways down to only 10 against the Friars.

"I think we learned a lot yesterday, and I think we executed better today than we did yesterday," Chandler said. "I think we still can go back and learn so much from today that we kind of fell into the same trap as yesterday, but I think we also showed a lot of growth."

For as excellent as BYU's offense was, Providence was just as good, shooting 57% from the field with 14 made triples in what was a true back-and-forth slugfest for 40 minutes.

But the Cougars' hustle made all the difference in escaping with a win, as they dominated on the offensive glass (11 rebounds to five) and won the battle for second chance points by a 13-3 margin.

Additionally, BYU cashed in 13 Providence turnovers for 15 points.

"I feel like that's the first thing we talk about on Day 1. We said we're going to be an offensive rebounding team," said Cougar forward Tyler Betsey. "Like, in practice, if we didn't crash (the glass), we would run, so that's a big emphasis on every game that we go into, and today it worked for us."

Added Young: "We built our team specific with spacing in mind, and tough guys that can still play defense and rebound."

In that regard, mission accomplished. At least for Wednesday.

"I felt really good about their desire to come in here and put that 'want-to' on the line, and I thought they did a great job," Young said.

"I thought the trio off our bench of Brooks Bahr, Nate Pickens and Khadim (Mboup), that's a trio that brings a ton of juice off the bench ... in terms of the 'want-to.' I thought the starters had it, and it kind of gets even more amplified when we sub."

Betsey enjoyed a career performance, posting 22 points and four rebounds while hitting six 3-pointers.

Not only was Betsey a mere 1 for 12 from long distance in Maui prior to Wednesday, but he was on the verge of missing the matchup altogether due to illness.

Instead, he played hero in helping the Cougars clinch a third-place tournament finish, and did so against a team that had tried to recruit him out of the transfer portal, as Friars coach Bryan Hodgson admitted postgame.

"I was getting the open shots I was getting all week (that) I haven't been hitting, but I trusted the work that I put in, and the ball just found the rim today," Betsey said.

Chandler continued his dominant, weeklong island effort with 24 points, five rebounds, six assists and five made 3s to cap a three-game stretch in which he averaged 27.3 points per contest and shot 58% from deep.

"I think he's really established himself as one of the premier guards in college basketball," Young said of his surging junior guard. "He has an extremely bright future at the next level because of how dynamic he is.

"He had six assists tonight. Granted we were making more shots, but last night he had zero assists. But I told him — and this is something I learned in the NBA — 'When you play with the ball in your hands a lot, with that comes a great responsibility,' so I thought he grew up in this tournament of understanding what that actually means."

With Chandler and Betsey's stat lines, BYU had its first pair of 20-point scorers since last year's Big 12 tournament.

In addition to them, Bruce Branch III recovered from a shaky Tuesday to score 13 points with six rebounds and two assists, with a late block on what would have been a go-ahead 3-pointer for Providence looming large in the narrow victory as well.

Dawson Baker hit a pair of 3s off the bench, Bahr grabbed four offensive boards and dished out five assists and Jaxon Kohler's triple in the final minute gave the Cougars a 5-point lead to extinguish a Providence rally.

There was still some late drama, as a desperation heave from the Friars cut their deficit to a single point with two seconds remaining, but Chandler knocked down two free throws to bury Providence for good.

Following its 2-1 Maui finish, BYU is 7-1 on the season and will now enjoy more than a week of rest before resuming its nonconference slate on Dec. 5 against Northwestern.

"Just extremely proud of the guys to dig down. Different guys had to step up. Collin put us on his back, really, this whole the tournament," Young said.

"... I'm just really proud of the group and think a lot of this adversity that we faced in this three-game deal can really — it's stuff we can build on as the season progresses."

articles.title: Noah Clowney, Egor Dëmin help Nets snap five-game skid with 104-97 win over Bucks
articles.summary: The trouble with measuring progress against the Milwaukee Bucks is that the Milwaukee Bucks are in considerably worse trouble than the Nets. Wednesday’s meet...
articles.body:
The trouble with measuring progress against the Milwaukee Bucks is that the Milwaukee Bucks are in considerably worse trouble than the Nets.

Wednesday's meeting at Fiserv Forum featured two teams with five combined victories, and much of the basketball reflected their respective places in the standings. Still, there were developments within Brooklyn's 104-97 victory worth taking seriously.

Noah Clowney played arguably his best game of the season. Egor Dëmin offered a compelling case for greater involvement in Brooklyn's half-court offense. And a team that's expected to keep searching for wins gave its fans something to enjoy on the night before Thanksgiving.

The Nets snapped a five-game losing streak and improved to 4-13.

Julius Randle led Brooklyn with 28 points and nine rebounds, but the complexion of the game changed with a pair of substitutions midway through the third quarter.

The Nets had squandered a 13-point first-half advantage and fallen behind by six when head coach Jordi Fernández turned to Dëmin and Clowney. Within two minutes, Dëmin had found Keon Ellis for a 3-pointer and delivered a pass to a cutting Day'Ron Sharpe for a dunk that put Brooklyn back in front.

The Nets outscored Milwaukee by 10 over the final 5:16 of the period.

Some of Dëmin's best work Wednesday came with the basketball in his hands. The difference between a point guard and a shooting guard seems increasingly irrelevant when evaluating a player with his combination of size and passing vision. What's important is how frequently Brooklyn puts him in positions to make decisions.

Dëmin finished with 15 points and four assists despite missing all five of his 3-point attempts. His ability to influence a game when his jumper isn't falling is precisely why the Nets should continue exploring the possibilities of playing him alongside Mikel Brown Jr., particularly with Nolan Traoré sidelined.

The two didn't share the floor Wednesday.

Brown, making his second career start, finished with six points on 2-for-9 shooting after scoring a career-high 17 points in the first half Monday in Minnesota.

Clowney, meanwhile, is beginning to put together some encouraging basketball. The 22-year-old scored nine of his 17 points in the fourth quarter, throwing down a driving dunk, knocking down a 3-pointer and converting a floater in the lane as Milwaukee tried to work its way back into the game.

The fourth-year forward shot 7-for-13 from the field, grabbed five rebounds and was a plus-22 with a little more than a minute remaining. Brooklyn was plus-14 in his nearly 27 minutes overall.

Ellis, whose recent performances have also been encouraging, contributed seven points, three assists and two steals. Grant Nelson grabbed six rebounds in 13 minutes, providing some much-needed size and energy behind Sharpe after Moritz Wagner was ruled out with left knee soreness.

Brooklyn's reserves accounted for 42 points.

Sharpe collected seven offensive rebounds and finished with 11 points, a season-high 14 rebounds, five assists, three steals and two blocks. His fifth double-double of the season matched his entire total from last year, leaving him one shy of his career high.

Michael Porter Jr. recorded his third double-double with 12 points, 11 rebounds and four assists, although he went scoreless in the second and third quarters after scoring eight points in the opening period.

The Nets shot just 41.6% from the field and 26.3% from deep, compensating with a 52-44 rebounding advantage and 24 points off Milwaukee turnovers. Tyler Herro scored 28 points and Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 21 for the Bucks, who fell to 2-17.

There were plenty of empty seats inside Fiserv Forum by the time Sharpe followed a missed Dëmin dunk with a putback that gave Brooklyn a 14-point advantage with 1:11 remaining.

It wasn't a particularly memorable night of NBA basketball. Still, for those invested in the future of the Nets, watching Clowney and Dëmin help put away an opponent made it a little more worthwhile.

Brooklyn continues its four-game road trip Friday against the Toronto Raptors.
authors: C.J. Holmes, New York Daily News

articles.title: Timberwolves beat the Thunder 113-106 to improve to 3-0 in NBA Cup play
articles.summary: OKLAHOMA CITY (AP) — Jaden McDaniels had 32 points and 10 rebounds, LaMelo Ball added 19 points before leaving with an ankle injury and the Minnesota Timberw...
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY (AP) — Jaden McDaniels had 32 points and 10 rebounds, LaMelo Ball added 19 points before leaving with an ankle injury and the Minnesota Timberwolves improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play with a 113-106 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday night.

Ball left the game in the the final 2:30 after landing on the foot of Thunder center Isaiah Hartenstein while they were fighting for a rebound.

Minnesota made 17 of 39 3-pointers (43.6%) and outrebounded the short-handed Thunder 40-30. Oklahoma City was playing without injured 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara (shin contusion).

McDaniels made 11 of 15 shots and was four of five from beyond the arc for the Timberwolves (14-5), who have won 12 of their last 12 games.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points and Ajay Mitchell added 25 for the Thunder (10-9), who have dropped six of nine amid the loss of three starters to long-term injuries.

Oklahoma City overcame a poor-shooting first quarter by outscoring the Timberwolves 37-21 in the second for a 53-47 halftime lead. Gilgeous-Alexander had 12 points in the quarter, including nine in the final three minutes.

The advantage grew to 73-63 on a 3-point play by SGA, but Minnesota responded with a 24-10 run to close out the third quarter. McDaniels made a pair of shots from distance, including a 26-footer at the buzzer to put the Timberwolves in front 87-83.

Oklahoma City pulled to within 105-104 on a 3-pointer by Mitchell but could not get any closer after that.

Timberwolves: Host Memphis on Friday night.

Thunder: Play at Milwaukee on Saturday night.

articles.title: College basketball expert calls Mark Pope a ‘major disappointment’
articles.summary: John Fanta didn't hold back in his criticism of Mark Pope, questioning Kentucky's roster construction.
articles.body:
Kentucky Basketball is off to a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, and the criticism surrounding Mark Pope and his program continues to grow following consecutive losses to Kansas by 20 points and Indiana by 14 points.

NBC Sports college basketball analyst John Fanta recently shared his thoughts on the state of Kentucky basketball, and he didn't hold back when discussing the third year of the Pope era.

"Let's just call it what it is: the Mark Pope era, to this point, has been a disappointment," Fanta said.

Fanta questioned Kentucky's defensive scheme, physicality, and overall roster construction, pointing to the Wildcats' struggles to stop opposing teams throughout the early portion of the season.

"Their defensive scheme, I'm not sure what it is. Scheme would be an exaggeration for what it actually is. They couldn't stop anybody early in the season. They couldn't stop Northern Arizona. They weren't going to stop Indiana. Milan Momcilovic, a winning player at a winning program, a lot is now on his shoulders. Too much is on his shoulders for a team with the kind of money that they possess. Their guards, not sturdy enough, not physical enough," Fanta said.

He also questioned whether Kentucky has the type of players necessary to meet the program's traditional expectations.

"When I think of Kentucky, I think of enforcers. They're not that. I like Malachi Moreno, but I look at this Kentucky roster, and I compare it to the resources that they are reported to have available. Mark Pope is not getting it done there."

Fanta continued his criticism by pointing to the expectations that come with coaching at Kentucky and the amount of money reportedly invested in the roster.

"To me, it comes off as he's trying to be someone that he actually isn't at a very difficult job. It's a hard job because they have high expectations, but you are judged on your record," he continued. "They had to claw just to get past Santa Clara in the NCAA Tournament with a $20 million roster. They spent a ton of money again. They're not getting it done."

Fanta ultimately believes Kentucky may need to make a change if things don't turn around, calling the current state of the program a major disappointment.

"The Mark Pope era is a major disappointment, and Kentucky is going to have to make a change. … It's just a brutal start to their season, and that fanbase has every right to be upset because, at Kentucky, if you want to be categorized as a blue blood—which the playing field has been level—it's a very, very big disappointment."

With Kentucky now facing increased pressure following its losses to Kansas and Indiana, Pope and the Wildcats have plenty of work to do to get the season back on track.

articles.title: Hornets lose sixth straight, fall narrowly to Bulls 107-105
articles.summary: Despite 22 lead changes, the Charlotte Hornets came out on the losing end once again, falling 107-105 to the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets faced the Chicago Bulls Wednesday in their final game before a brief Thanksgiving break. Charlotte entered the contest 4-12, having suffered losses in 11 of their last 12 contests. Both teams would play without key contributors, as the home team was missing Grayson Allen, Ryan Kalkbrenner, Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder. The Bulls were without Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell and Jalen Smith, who was originally listed as questionable with an illness.

Both teams were evenly matched, as the game went back-and-forth throughout, with 22 lead changes and neither side leading by more than eight points. Entering the fourth quarter with a two-point deficit, the Hornets were unable to get the job done, as Coby White missed a difficult step-back two-pointer, which would have tied the game in the final seconds, as the Hornets fell 107-105. With the loss, Charlotte went winless in NBA Cup Group Play.

Brandon Miller led the team with 35 points on 13-for-25 shooting to go along with three rebounds, one assist and three steals. Rookie Christian Anderson Jr. had 15 points, four assists and one rebound off the bench with zero turnovers, while Moussa Diabate tallied a 14-point, 14-rebound double-double. Chicago finished with seven scorers in double figures, including Matas Buzelis, who scored 24. Now losers of six in a row, the Hornets will host the Brooklyn Nets Saturday.

articles.title: Nets snap 5-game skid with 104-97 win over Bucks
articles.summary: The trouble with measuring progress against the Milwaukee Bucks is that the Milwaukee Bucks are in considerably worse trouble than the Brooklyn Nets. Wednesd...
articles.body:
The trouble with measuring progress against the Milwaukee Bucks is that the Milwaukee Bucks are in considerably worse trouble than the Brooklyn Nets.

Wednesday's meeting at Fiserv Forum featured two teams with five combined victories, and much of the basketball reflected their respective places in the standings. Still, there were developments within Brooklyn's 104-97 victory worth taking seriously.

Noah Clowney played arguably his best game of the season. Egor Dëmin offered a compelling case for greater involvement in Brooklyn's half-court offense. And a team that's expected to keep searching for wins gave its fans something to enjoy on the night before Thanksgiving.

The Nets snapped a five-game losing streak and improved to 4-13.

Julius Randle led Brooklyn with 28 points and nine rebounds, but the complexion of the game changed with a pair of substitutions midway through the third quarter.

The Nets had squandered a 13-point first-half advantage and fallen behind by six when head coach Jordi Fernández turned to Dëmin and Clowney. Within two minutes, Dëmin had found Keon Ellis for a 3-pointer and delivered a pass to a cutting Day'Ron Sharpe for a dunk that put Brooklyn back in front.

The Nets outscored Milwaukee by 10 over the final 5:16 of the period.

Some of Dëmin's best work Wednesday came with the basketball in his hands. The difference between a point guard and a shooting guard seems increasingly irrelevant when evaluating a player with his combination of size and passing vision. What's important is how frequently Brooklyn puts him in positions to make decisions.

Dëmin finished with 15 points and four assists despite missing all five of his 3-point attempts. His ability to influence a game when his jumper isn't falling is precisely why the Nets should continue exploring the possibilities of playing him alongside Mikel Brown Jr., particularly with Nolan Traoré sidelined.

The two didn't share the floor Wednesday.

Brown, making his second career start, finished with six points on 2-for-9 shooting after scoring a career-high 17 points in the first half Monday in Minnesota.

Clowney, meanwhile, is beginning to put together some encouraging basketball. The 22-year-old scored nine of his 17 points in the fourth quarter, throwing down a driving dunk, knocking down a 3-pointer and converting a floater in the lane as Milwaukee tried to work its way back into the game.

The fourth-year forward shot 7 for 13 from the field, grabbed five rebounds and was a plus-22 with a little more than a minute remaining. Brooklyn was plus-14 in his nearly 27 minutes overall.

Ellis, whose recent performances have also been encouraging, contributed seven points, three assists and two steals. Grant Nelson grabbed six rebounds in 13 minutes, providing some much-needed size and energy behind Sharpe after Moritz Wagner was ruled out with left knee soreness.

Brooklyn's reserves accounted for 42 points.

Sharpe collected seven offensive rebounds and finished with 11 points, a season-high 14 rebounds, five assists, three steals and two blocks. His fifth double-double of the season matched his entire total from last year, leaving him one shy of his career high.

Michael Porter Jr. recorded his third double-double with 12 points, 11 rebounds and four assists, although he went scoreless in the second and third quarters after scoring eight points in the opening period.

The Nets shot just 41.6% from the field and 26.3% from deep, compensating with a 52-44 rebounding advantage and 24 points off Milwaukee turnovers. Tyler Herro scored 28 points and Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 21 for the Bucks, who fell to 2-17.

There were plenty of empty seats inside Fiserv Forum by the time Sharpe followed a missed Dëmin dunk with a putback that gave Brooklyn a 14-point advantage with 1:11 remaining.

It wasn't a particularly memorable night of NBA basketball. Still, for those invested in the future of the Nets, watching Clowney and Dëmin help put away an opponent made it a little more worthwhile.

Brooklyn continues its four-game road trip Friday against the Toronto Raptors.
authors: C.J. Holmes, New York Daily News

articles.title: Kristian Winfield: Knicks win 6th in a row after another Cavaliers meltdown
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Call it the New York Knickerbocker special — because when the Knicks are down big, they’ve got their opponent right where they want them. Especial...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Call it the New York Knickerbocker special — because when the Knicks are down big, they've got their opponent right where they want them. Especially when that opponent is the Cleveland Cavaliers, who naturally have a propensity for blowing leads in the playoffs and the regular season. The Knicks would know best as the team that embarrassed them in a four-game sweep in the Eastern Conference finals on their way to the NBA title last season.

Thanksgiving Eve was reminiscent of those scrappy games that quickly became synonymous with the Knicks' title run: The Knicks — without OG Anunoby (calf), Miles McBride (adductor) and Jordan Clarkson (foot), plus a limited Jalen Brunson (illness) and Karl-Anthony Towns (knee) — came out sluggish in their NBA Cup matchup against the Cavaliers and trailed at the half despite 17 early points from Mikal Bridges.

And then the Cavs did what they do best: They collapsed. Fell apart. Folded like a lawn chair set up around the Thanksgiving table. The Knicks erased an 11-point lead and found themselves up nearly 20 in an eventual 121 victory at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday.

They are now 1-2 in NBA Cup play and boast a 12-6 record as winners of six in a row and 10 of their last 12 games.

It's an all-too familiar pattern between the two Eastern Conference foes since Brunson and Donovan Mitchell each completed their relocations from the Western Conference. The Cavs have blown two double-digit leads against the Knicks since Brunson arrived in New York in the summer of 2022: a 17-point lead last Christmas and the notorious Game 1 of the conference finals, a game the Cavs led by as many as 22 points before ceding an unprecedented 44-11 run to lose by 11 in overtime. Cleveland also led by eight in the third quarter of a Jan. 2023 matchup against the Knicks and went on to lose by two.

And then there are the incomplete rallies: the games the Knicks have held a double-digit lead, blown them, then held on to win regardless. This has occurred 13 times in the Brunson-and-Mitchell era, including seven times where the Cavs either overtook or tied a double-digit lead — and still went on to lose the game.

Wednesday added another chapter with the NBA Cup guidelines promoting a blowout score. The Knicks won the fourth quarter, 39-17, after winning the third quarter by only two points.

And the spark behind it all? Jose Alvarado, who his three 3s inside of the first three-and-a-half minutes of the final frame. Alvarado shot five-of-seven from deep and finished with 21 points. The Knicks outscored the Cavs by 15 points in the reserve guard's 19 minutes on the floor.

"We know we're the best bench in the league," Alvarado said in his walk-off interview. "And we have to go out there and play like it."

The Knicks bench scored 45 of their 121 points on Wednesday. Brunson scored 19 points on 6-of-22 shooting from the field, and Karl-Anthony Towns recorded his 17th consecutive double double with 12 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists. Landry Shamet added 11 points and Josh Hart scored 15 points to go with 12 assists and seven rebounds. All five Knicks starters scored in double figures, while Mitchell (30 points) and James Harden (28) combined for 58 points but got just 54 from their teammates.

The Knicks do not play on Thanksgiving but host the Miami Heat on Friday in another NBA Cup game.
authors: Kristian Winfield, New York Daily News

articles.title: Nets topple Bucks in NBA Cup clash to snap five-game skid
articles.summary: Julius Randle netted a team-high 28 points as the Nets (4-13) posted their first NBA Cup win this season after losses against the Pistons and the Magic.
articles.body:
The teams with the two worst records in the Eastern Conference faced each other Wednesday night in Milwaukee, but no one needed to accuse either the Nets or the Bucks of tanking in this one.

Neither team can win the draft lottery after the season because both franchises essentially traded their respective 2027 first-round picks years ago, but the Nets at least halted their five-game losing streak with a defensively improved 104-97 victory in an NBA Cup game at Fiserv Forum.

Julius Randle netted a team-high 28 points as the Nets (4-13) posted their first NBA Cup victory after losses earlier in the season against the Pistons and the Magic.

Michael Porter Jr. was held to 12 points on 4-for-14 shooting with 11 rebounds to follow another quiet scoring night (11) Monday in Minnesota.

Egor Dëmin had an active game with 14 points and a plus-15 rating in 25 minutes off the bench.

Noah Clowney nailed three 3-pointers among his 17 points, and Day'Ron Sharpe contributed 11 points, 14 boards and five assists for the Nets.

Tyler Herro, who had a career-best 50-point game Saturday against the 76ers, scored 21 of his 28 points in the second half for the Bucks (2-17).

"We've lost a few in a row, so we've gotta try to get a win no matter who we're playing against," Porter told the YES Network before the game. "They're an NBA team. They are at the bottom of the standings right now, but so are we, so it's gonna be a dogfight, and we gotta try to get out of here with a win."

The NBA instituted rule changes in the offseason to discourage tanking for draft position, essentially penalizing the teams with the worst three records in the league with lower odds to secure the No. 1 overall pick in the lottery.

The Nets' 2027 first-round pick is controlled by the Rockets from an unprotected pick swap as part of Brooklyn's deal to acquire James Harden in January 2021.

The Bucks, who dealt away superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat over the summer, also had committed to a pick swap involving their 2027 first-rounder when they acquired guard Jrue Holiday from New Orleans in 2020.

The Nets had allowed at least 70 points in the first half four times during their five-game skid, but this slow start was more due to offensive inefficiency.

Brooklyn missed five of its first six shots and spotted the Bucks a 9-2 lead in the first three minutes.

But Porter knocked down two straight 3s and scored eight as part of a 15-1 run to vault the Nets into an eight-point advantage en route to a 28-24 edge through 12 minutes.

A 3-pointer by Clowney and a jumper by Randle extended the cushion to 10 early in the second. The Nets led by as many as 13 before the Bucks closed within 51-47 before intermission.

"We have to close quarters better," Randle, who had 16 in the half, told YES.

Rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. scored all six of his points in the second half after posting 17 in his first NBA start Monday in Minnesota.

Dëmin came off the bench again and contributed five points before halftime, including a driving bucket through the lane in the closing minute.

Herro only managed seven points in the first half, but his 3-pointer pulled the Bucks even, 53-53, early in the third quarter.

Brown finally recorded his first two buckets after seven misses to push Brooklyn back ahead, and two late dunks by Sharpe and a traditional three-point play by Dëmin helped the Nets carry a 77-71 edge into the final quarter.

Keon Ellis (plus-14) and Grant Nelson provided some defensive energy off the bench to open the fourth, and Porter converted an and-1 to stretch the lead back to 11 with 10:38 remaining.

Moritz Wagner didn't play in the second half due to what the Nets said was left knee soreness.
